$comment: Single declarative manifest of the blueprint's required structure. Read by check-structure.ps1 and check-structure.sh so the required-path list exists once, as data, instead of twice, as code. Add a path here when you add a required file; nothing else needs to change.
$requiredFilesComment: What the blueprint layer guarantees. README.md is deliberately absent: a project's README is its own identity, not something the blueprint provides or requires. .gitignore IS required, because sync seeds it -- an adopted project without one is a secret waiting to be committed.

distribution.$comment: The portable/project-specific split, declared once as data. sync-blueprint copies only 'portable' paths and never touches 'projectSpecific' ones. Getting this wrong overwrites a project's own facts, so the split lives here rather than being restated in two scripts.
distribution.$sourceOnlyComment: Tooling for RELEASING ForgeOS, not for building with it. It lives inside a portable directory because the discovery gate permits writes only to .ai/ docs/ .claude/ scripts/ templates/ examples/ .github/ -- a new top-level tools/ is refused in an undefined project, and every permitted home except docs/ is distributed. So the split needs a third state: carried by the repository, never copied into a project. sync-blueprint drops these paths from the portable set before classifying, check-links stops requiring their references to travel, and check-policy fails if the declaration is contradicted elsewhere in this file. This is a STRENGTHENING: fewer files reach an adopter, never more. It is also how the release workflow will be handled -- .github/workflows IS portable, so a release.yml placed there would be copied into every adopting project and try to release theirs.
distribution.$licenseComment: LICENSE is project-specific and is deliberately NOT in requiredFiles or seedFiles. Syncing it would copy this repository's copyright holder into someone else's project, and requiring it would fail check-structure for every adopter that has not chosen a licence yet. A project's licence is its own decision.
distribution.$projectSpecificComment: Never written by sync once present. .ai/context holds facts only the project knows; tasks, plans, and memory are its history; docs are its source of truth; blueprint.version records what it adopted.
distribution.$seedComment: SEEDED ONCE, THEN NEVER TOUCHED AGAIN. A brand-new project has none of the project-specific half, so the discovery gate would find no .ai/context/project.md to read, check-placeholders would report 0 blocking, and the gate would fail open on the exact case it exists for. These files are copied only when absent. An existing file is never compared, never overwritten, never reported.
distribution.$seedTemplatesComment: A seed file is normally copied from the source path of the same name. That is wrong for any file that holds the BLUEPRINTS OWN answers: project.md carried its identity (v1.10.1 -- including Profile none, which silently disables the profile role evidence finish-task enforces), and constraints.md carries its real constraints since v1.12.1. A mapped target is seeded from its template instead, so an adopting project starts undefined and answers for itself.
distribution.$seedDirectoriesComment: Created empty with a generated .gitkeep. Their blueprint contents are the blueprint's own history and must not travel into a project.

policy.$comment: Controls that live in .claude/settings.json rather than in a hook, because the harness enforces them with zero process startup. check-policy verifies they are actually present -- a control that moved out of a tested hook must not become untested.
policy.$contextBudgetComment: The always-loaded context and its budget, as data. First written as prose in .ai/context/README.md at v1.9.0, where nothing could read it; check-context-budget reads THIS block and reports against it on every check-all run. Informational -- it warns, it does not gate. Since v1.12.3 the files are classified: platformFiles is the floor the blueprint itself imposes and a project cannot reduce, projectFiles is what the project owns and can trim. The project's allowance is derived -- targetTokens minus the measured platform floor -- so an overrun is attributed to its owner instead of blaming whoever happens to run the check. Tokens are estimated as characters divided by charsPerToken; re-measure before arguing with a number.
policy.$profileComplianceComment: A profile declared roles and nothing ever checked that a project honoured them -- risk R-25. Enforcing every required role on every task would be worse: a review with nothing to examine teaches people to sign off without looking. So enforcement is the intersection of two declarations. The TASK declares which areas it touches; the PROFILE decides which of those areas demand a role. A docs-only task tagged 'none' owes nothing. Tags are validated against this list, because a typo that silently disables a security review is exactly the failure this is meant to prevent.

profileCompliance.$sectionComment: Where finish-task reads the declaration. Parsed fields, never free prose: the agent states the tags and the evidence, and the script checks that a tag demanding a role has a matching evidence line.
profileCompliance.$promotedFieldComment: A promotion used to be inferred from prose, and the inference was order-dependent: the PowerShell parser required the word promoted BEFORE the role name, so `security-reviewer` is promoted... was invisible to it while the POSIX one saw it. A structured field removes the guess. The prose form is still read as a fallback, order-insensitively, but only names that appear in scopeRoles are accepted -- otherwise a backticked profile name on the same line would be mistaken for a role.

policy.$publicSurfaceComment: The public launch surface, as data. required = what must exist for the repository to be publishable at all; expected = the trust files the M-19.1 launch contract demands before it goes public, absent today and reported as advisory drift until the surface slices write them. claimFile is the page whose numeric claims are audited against what the tools report -- it announced version 1.13.4 at v1.15.1, which is the drift this check exists for. sections are the two tables that make the proof table believable: a claim table with no counterpart is marketing. NONE of these files may ever be portable or seeded: an adopting project that inherited SECURITY.md would publish this repository's disclosure address as its own.

publicSurface.$expectedComment: Where these live is not a preference. guard-discovery permits writes only to .ai/ docs/ .claude/ scripts/ templates/ examples/ .github/ -- a root SECURITY.md is refused by this project's own gate, the same refusal that gave scripts/release its home in v1.15.0. .github/ is where GitHub looks for community health files anyway, so the gate and the convention agree; the two content pages live in docs/, which the gate permits and sync never touches.

policy.$entrypointsComment: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are the only files an agent is guaranteed to read, which makes them the most tempting place to restate a rule 'for salience' -- and the least visible place for that copy to drift. It already happened: AGENTS.md carried 7 of the 8 non-negotiable rules from core.md section 3, and the 8th had silently gone missing. Same defect as the .claude/ adapters, caught two versions later only because nothing was checking. maxLines 40 is derived: after the v1.8.2 rewrite CLAUDE.md is 31 lines and AGENTS.md 37, so 40 leaves room for a pointer, not for a rules section.

entrypoints.$forbiddenPatternsComment: Deliberately dumb, and written to work identically in .NET regex and POSIX ERE: [ \t] rather than \s. It matches the shape of the non-negotiable list itself -- a numbered line beginning with 'Never' -- which is exactly how the drifted copy was written.

policy.$requiredHookScriptsComment: Event presence is not wiring. A settings file can declare PreToolUse and still reference no guard, so each hook script is named here and check-policy asserts the settings file references it.
policy.$discoveryGateComment: Enforces core.md section 0. While any blocking placeholderScan target still carries a marker, guard-discovery blocks Write/Edit outside these paths. The allowlist is everything discovery and adoption legitimately write, plus the blueprint's own surfaces -- so a maintainer is never locked out of the blueprint itself. Everything else is where a project's source, manifests, and scaffolding would land.

adapter.$comment: The load-bearing constraint of this blueprint: .claude/ is an adapter, not a home for rules. Every adapter file must point into .ai/. Without this check the constraint is documentation only, which is the weak kind of mitigation.
adapter.$pairingComment: An adapter with no source in .ai/ is a second knowledge source by definition -- there is nowhere else its content could have come from. A source with no adapter is a role Claude Code cannot dispatch, which quietly makes the role advisory. Both directions are failures, so both are checked.
adapter.$thinComment: Referencing .ai/ was not enough. Before v1.2.0 every agent and skill adapter referenced its source AND restated it in different words -- 1.6x to 2.1x the size of the file it pointed at, with zero literal duplicate lines, so no diff could reveal the drift. Commands had the same defect at 329 lines across 10 files. Limits are derived from measurement, not taste, and differ per surface because the surfaces differ: a role adapter needs a pointer, a slash command legitimately needs concrete invocations for two shells.

thin.name: agents-and-skills
thin.$comment: After the v1.2.0 rewrite these are 8-10 lines, 0.23x-0.33x their sources. maxLines 20 is double the observed maximum -- room for a longer description, nowhere near enough to smuggle a Method section back in.

thin.name: commands
thin.$comment: A slash command needs more room than a role adapter: it carries the concrete PowerShell and bash invocations, which a workflow file cannot. After the v1.2.1 rewrite the 10 commands are 10-21 lines (was 27-40) and carry ZERO '##' headings -- a command that needs sections is restating a procedure that belongs in .ai/workflows/. maxLines 35 leaves room for a command with several invocations; the heading rule is what actually bites.

sourceOfTruth.$comment: v1.3.1 made docs/ the source of truth for project facts and reduced .ai/context/ to linked operational summaries. That rule was documentation only. Every rule this repository left to documentation alone has broken -- adapter discipline, command adapters, the finish-task gate count: three for three. These two guards are deliberately dumb. They check that the pointer phrase is present and that a small list of known-duplicated headings has not come back. They cannot detect a paraphrase, and are not meant to.

summaries.$forbiddenComment: Section titles owned by docs/. Their reappearance in a context summary is the exact shape the v1.3.1 refactor removed.

profiles.$comment: A profile names roles and points at documents. Two ways it can rot: naming a role that does not exist, which makes the profile a lie; or restating what docs/ owns, which makes it a second source of truth. Roles are declared in frontmatter rather than prose so the check is exact instead of clever -- a regex over prose would guess, and a guessing check produces false positives.

openQuestions.$markersComment: An operational file may mention an assumption or an open question, but it must send the reader to the register in the same file. Otherwise the knowledge lands somewhere nobody will look.
openQuestions.$exemptComment: The register itself, and templates and examples, which exist to show the shape of a record rather than to instruct.

linkCheck.$comment: Repository-relative paths referenced from Markdown must resolve. A reference to a file that does not exist sends an agent somewhere empty and costs a whole turn.

placeholderScan.$comment: Directories scanned by check-placeholders for unfilled TBD markers, with the adoption weight of each. Weight reflects how much an unfilled fact degrades agent behavior.

targets.note: Agents load these every session. Unfilled means every task starts blind, and the discovery gate stays closed.
The source of truth for requirements.
Needed for correct naming and business rules.
runbook and deployment are executed under pressure, during an incident. A TBD there is a missing procedure, not a documentation gap. Raised from medium in v1.3.1.
Needed only for projects with a user interface.

placeholderScan.$markersComment: Matched as whole words, so TBD, TBD:, TBD., and TBD, all count. Do not add a colon here.
placeholderScan.$bracketComment: A second placeholder convention exists in the templates: bracketed prompts such as [modular monolith / microservices], [requirements and approach], [stores]. docs/architecture/overview.md is written entirely in that style -- 49 of them, zero TBD -- so before v1.3.0 the readiness score reported docs/architecture as needing only 4 markers, all from decisions.md, while the single most important architecture document sat completely unfilled and unmeasured. The score was not merely incomplete; it was misleading. Markdown links are excluded by the negative lookahead, and fenced code blocks are skipped so that array[index] in a sample is not mistaken for a gap.
placeholderScan.$bracketCaseComment: The class is written [A-Za-z] rather than [a-z] on purpose. PowerShell's -match is case-insensitive by default and grep -E is case-sensitive, so [a-z] silently matched [Component Name] on Windows and skipped it on POSIX -- a 10-line divergence between the two platforms from one pattern relying on engine defaults. Spell the intent; do not inherit it.
